prompt:
Create a high-fidelity portrait mobile web homepage for Farls da bag, a public fantasy football league museum. Render a 390×844 CSS viewport at high resolution, edge to edge, with crisp readable text and no surrounding device or browser. Visitors discover all-time achievements and disasters, then open their supporting records.

Lead with one dominant stacked all-time record slate. Reading order is league masthead, functional navigation, provenance, slate, direct archive actions, and the start of recent history. The slate says "All-time records" and shows the selected scope "Regular season". Its first linked entry is "Uncrowned Kings", "Northside", "2024", "+24% vs league average", "14 games". Its second linked entry is "Bench Crimes", "Fourth & Regret", "2023 week 7", "38.7 bench points". Make the metrics the visual evidence and retain their units. Use these synthetic examples only. Clearly show "Design preview · synthetic records".

The frame has "Farls da bag" as its masthead and navigation links "Records", "Exhibits", "Menu". Below the slate provide unmistakable "Record book" and "Exhibits" actions. Begin a distinct "Recent history" section, with a linked "2024 · Northside" entry visible.

Sunday football broadcast graphics provide the page's structure: a silver broadcast field, substantial navy score strips, flat red emphasis, sturdy football broadcast sans lettering and tabular numerals. The stacked slate is the one expressive move; surrounding navigation and history remain quiet in the same materials. It must read as a working website. No tagline, helper copy, invented league statistics, champion, trophy, headshot, generic headline-and-card hero, or poster.
